channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Japanese Yen strengthens on US bond buyback, traders brace for US PCE inflation report
item.description: The USD/JPY pair loses ground to near 158.90 during the Asian trading hours on Wednesday. The US Treasury’s bond buyback programs weigh on the US Dollar (USD) against the Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: Australian Dollar strengthens against Japanese Yen following CPI data
item.description: AUD/JPY gains ground for the second consecutive day, trading around 114.20 during the Asian hours on Wednesday.

item.title: BoJ to raise rate to 1.25% in September — Reuters poll
item.description: According to August 17-24 survey in a Reuters poll, 57% of economists expected the Bank of Japan (BoJ) to raise its interest rate in September, a sharp turnaround from a July poll.

item.title: Australia’s CPI inflation declines to 3.5% YoY in July vs. 3.2% forecast
item.description: Australia’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose by 3.5% year-over-year (YoY) in July, compared to a 3.8% growth reported in June, the latest data published by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) showed on Wednesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar strengthens after hot CPI report; eyes multi-month high ahead of US PCE
item.description: The AUD/USD pair attracts buyers for the second straight day and climbs to the 0.7170 area following the release of Australian consumer inflation figures during the Asian session on Wednesday.

item.title: WTI drops amid Middle East diplomacy, eased US sanction fears
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price extends its losses for the third consecutive day, trading around $80.10 per barrel during the Asian hours on Wednesday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar weakens amid falling oil prices as USD holds steady ahead of US PCE
item.description: The USD/CAD pair edges higher during the Asian session on Wednesday, though it remains confined within the previous day’s range. Spot prices currently trade around mid-1.3800s as traders now look to the US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index for some meaningful impetus.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7829 vs. 6.7852 previous
item.description: On Wednesday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7829 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7852 and 6.7166 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Euro steadies above 1.1650 ahead of US PCE data
item.description: The EUR/USD pair flatlines near 1.1675 during the early Asian trading hours on Wednesday. The US Treasury's decision to expand its long-term bond buyback program could weigh on the US Dollar (USD) against the Euro (EUR).

item.title: Canada announces 'dollar-for-dollar' retaliatory tariffs up to 50% against US
item.description: Canada said that it will implement 50% retaliatory tariffs on $20bn worth of US goods, following through on Prime Minister Mark Carney’s vow to match US President Donald Trump’s duties “dollar for dollar,” the Guardian reported.

item.title: Iran and Oman push talks for ‘interim’ reopening of Hormuz — Bloomberg
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his Omani counterpart Badr Albusaidi discussed an “interim framework” aimed at resuming shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold advances above $4,650 on US Dollar weakness, Treasury bond buyback plans
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) rises to around $4,670, the highest since May 14, during the early Asian session on Wednesday. The precious metal extends the rally amid a weaker US Dollar (USD) and as the US Treasury’s bond buyback plans.

item.title: Australian Dollar rises after RBA hawkish minutes, inflation data eyed
item.description: The Aussie Dollar advanced on Tuesday, gaining over 0.20% as the Greenback edged lower, amid minutes from the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA)'s last meeting suggesting the board was close to raising rates. At the time of writing, the AUD/USD trades at 0.7163, after bouncing off daily lows of 0.7137.

item.title: Tokyo bought the Japanese Yen a range, not a trend
item.description: USD/JPY trades just above 159.00 late on Tuesday, August 25, holding a gain of under a tenth of a percent across a session that has covered 44 pips between a floor near 159.00 and a ceiling short of 159.50.

item.title: Pound Sterling's six-month high has no British test this week
item.description: GBP/USD trades near 1.3650 late on Tuesday, August 25, up around a tenth of a percent on a session that has covered barely 33 pips between a floor just above 1.3600 and a ceiling a shade over 1.3650.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Consolidation risk after recent gains against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong expect USD/SGD to consolidate as earlier Singapore Dollar (SGD) gains face a modest US Dollar (USD) rebound and position unwinding ahead of United States (US) core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index data and Jackson Hole.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Bulls hold 217.00 after trendline break
item.description: The GBP/JPY surpassed a downtrend resistance line and reclaimed the 217.00 level on Tuesday, as the Japanese Yen weakened while Sterling pushed to a new three-week high at 217.48. At the time of writing, the cross-pair trades at 217.31, up 0.20%.

item.title: Mexican Peso holds below 16.95 as traders eye US data, Iran shift
item.description: The Mexican Peso holds firm near 10-year highs against the US Dollar on Tuesday, as the USD/MXN pair sits below the 16.95 level while investors digest US economic data and recent developments between the US and Iran. The exotic pair trades at 16.94, virtually unchanged.

item.title: Thai Baht: Bullish bias against US Dollar faces BoT sensitivity – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that Thai Baht (THB) has rallied to a two‑month high on softer US Dollar (USD), lower Oil prices, strong electronics exports and Gold-related flows.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Bullish bias with focus on 6.7000 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann maintain a negative stance on USD/CNH, noting a softened underlying tone even as recent price action stayed relatively quiet. Intraday, they see scope for a modest drift lower while keeping 6.7150 as key support.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar climbs to fresh highs amid timid US Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD climbed to around 0.5980 Tuesday, near its highest level since June 1 as a softer US Dollar (USD) and firm Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) rate-hike expectations powered the Kiwi higher.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Range-bound consolidation outlook against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay and Dr. Henry Hao note that USD/SGD has eased from 1.2800 to around 1.2700 as the softer US Dollar (USD) and global risk sentiment dominate.

item.title: US-Iran agree ceasefire deal, sinks Oil – RIA Novosti
item.description: The Russian agency RIA Novosti reported on Tuesday that Washington and Tehran agreed to a ceasefire, citing sources in Iran and Pakistan.

item.title: US Treasury yields fall as Hormuz progress eases inflation fears
item.description: US yields edge lower across the whole curve on Tuesday, following suit.

item.title: South Korean Won: Strength backed by tech flows against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts highlight that the Korean Won (KRW) has gained 12% versus the Dollar year-to-date, with USD/KRW falling from around 1560 in June to below 1380.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Trade risks limit gains against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that reports of potential US tariffs on Chinese goods and the PBoC’s resistance to rapid Renminbi (RMB) gains are likely to limit further downside in USD/CNH.

item.title: The US Dollar Index stops paying for hawks who cannot vote
item.description: A non-voting regional Federal Reserve president published a conditional hold on Tuesday, tying the current target range to continued evidence that inflation is actually coming down, and the Dollar Index has not moved for it.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar stays on the back foot ahead of PCE
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) is hovering below the 99.00 mark as traders squared positions ahead of a heavy Wednesday data slate and Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address on Friday.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Upside momentum eases against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD remains under mild downward pressure but short-term momentum is flat, keeping the pair in a tight intraday band around 1.2700.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD reclaims 100-day SMA, eyes $70
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price registers modest gains on Tuesday, after briefly breaching the 100-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) at $68.38, pushing the white metal to a three-day low of $67.43 before making a U-turn and turning bullish. The XAG/USD pair trades at $68.86, up 0.55%,
